runs.text:
Here's what we believe, plainly: everyone is created equal. Everyone has certain basic rights that no one can take away. These include the right to live, to be free, and to seek happiness.

Governments exist to protect these rights. They only have power because the people agree to be governed.

If a government starts working against these rights, the people have the right to change it or get rid of it. They can then set up a new government, built on ideas and rules that seem most likely to keep them safe and happy.

To be sure, you shouldn't overthrow a long-standing government for small or short-term reasons. History shows that people tend to put up with problems, even bad ones, rather than fix things by scrapping the system they're used to.

But when a government repeatedly abuses its power and takes away people's rights, always aiming for the same goal, it shows that the government wants total control. At that point, people have both the right and the duty to overthrow that government. They must then build new safeguards to protect their future.
